name: placeholder-shown
summary: Styles an input while its placeholder is visible, which is how a floating label knows the field is empty.
caveats: `:placeholder-shown` only matches a field that **has** a placeholder. For the floating label pattern the field usually shows no placeholder text of its own, and the way round that is `placeholder=" "`, a single space, which keeps the pseudo-class working while showing nothing.

The pseudo-class goes on the selector the mixin is called in, so it needs one. Called at the root it wrote `&:placeholder-shown`, which the page described as styling every field and which styles none of them: measured in Chrome 152, Firefox 156 and Safari 26.6.2, all three keep the rule and an empty input holds its own border while `matches(":placeholder-shown")` answers true, because a top-level `&` is `:scope` and that is the document. Dart Sass 1.91's command line refuses it outright, so the same call is a build error or dead CSS depending on how the stylesheet is compiled. Both that and a call with no block raise since 4.0.0; `all-text-inputs` is the way to reach every field.
